description:
UMBRELLA for the HTR-10 thermal-spectrum critical path. Audit 2026-08-11.

QUESTION ANSWERED: yes, njoy-outram-park-fork is the correct owner of S(alpha,beta) — root CLAUDE.md puts all cross-section/nuclear-data code there and keeps transport crates data-free, and the code already follows that (thermr reads MF=7; outram-mc-libs holds no ENDF parsing and builds its ThermalScattering from the njoy surface).

WHAT ALREADY WORKS (verified by running the port against ENDF/B-VIII.0, not by reading docs):
  - MF=7 parsing of all three graphite evaluations: tsl-crystalline-graphite (MAT=30), tsl-reactor-graphite-10P (MAT=31), -30P (MAT=32). All report coherent_elastic=true, incoherent_elastic=false, incoherent_inelastic=true.
  - Coherent-elastic sigma(E) with correct physics: zero below the Bragg cutoff, first edge at 1.83e-3 eV (graphite (002)), 24 open reflections at 0.0253 eV, sigma_coh_el(0.0253) = 4.55 b.
  - Incoherent-inelastic sigma_inel(E) reaching the free-atom limit (4.61 b at 3.9 eV vs B(1) = 4.739 b), and a 16-bin equiprobable emission table.
  - THERMR is REAL, not a scaffold: coherent, incoherent-elastic and incoherent-inelastic all implemented (~1.4k lines across src/thermr/). Only thermr::run(), the NJOY card-input driver, is NotPorted — the typed module API is the intended entry point.

DATA IS AVAILABLE OFFLINE: /home/teddy0/Documents/research/ENDF-B-VIII.0/thermal_scatt/ holds all three graphite tapes plus their .leapr decks and .readme provenance. reference-data/endf/ in-repo holds only a README (no tapes). LEAPR is therefore NOT on the critical path — the S(alpha,beta) already exists and does not need generating.

THE GAP IS THE LAST MILE, AND IT IS TOTAL: crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/ has ZERO references to thermal scattering (grep for thermal/ThermalScattering/with_thermal returns nothing across delta_tracking.rs, keff_delta.rs, mod.rs, sphere_packing.rs). The pebble-bed graphite matrix is currently pure free-gas.

ORDERED BLOCKERS:
  1. op-h23 — carbon in well_known_mat. DONE 2026-08-11 (C-12 MAT=625, C-13 MAT=628, verified against the tapes).
  2. op-1y4y — coherent-elastic extra-temperature S(E) tables are discarded; sigma_coh_el only at 296 K. Hard blocker for the 120/250 C benchmark points and all hot operation.
  3. op-u5ju — njoy consumer surface for the elastic channels.
  4. op-nhoa — outram-mc ThermalScattering elastic channel + sampling.
  5. THIS BEAD — wire it into pebble_beds material construction and add an HTR-10 graphite thermal-spectrum V&V case.

Also relevant: op-cjw.22 (inelastic temperature interpolation) is filed P4 on the stated assumption that 'target temps (293.6K) are tabulated exactly'. That assumption FAILS for HTR-10: requested 393 K and 523 K snap to tabulated 400 K and 500 K, a 23 K error at the 250 C point. Consider re-prioritising.

DO NOT describe HTR-10 neutronics as validated until this closes.

notes.content:
BLOCKER 4 (op-nhoa) IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-11, uncommitted. Ordered-blocker status is now: 1 op-h23 DONE; 2 op-1y4y fixed and COMMITTED (in 4feb6c84); 3 op-u5ju done and COMMITTED (thermr::scattering exposes all three channels); 4 op-nhoa IMPLEMENTED THIS SESSION - outram-mc ThermalScattering now carries the elastic channel and Nuclide::xs_at_energy substitutes sigma_inel + sigma_el, with 7 V&V tests green against ENDF/B-VIII.0 graphite (see the op-nhoa comment for the measured numbers); 5 THIS BEAD - pebble_beds wiring + an HTR-10 graphite thermal-spectrum V&V case - STILL OPEN AND UNTOUCHED.

Re-verified this session that step 5's gap is still total: grep for thermal/ThermalScattering/with_thermal across crates/outram-mc-libs/src/pebble_beds/{delta_tracking,keff_delta,mod,sphere_packing,references}.rs still returns nothing. The pebble-bed graphite matrix remains pure free-gas, so examples/htr10_fuel_zone_kinf.rs and anything built on run_keff_delta are still disqualified as physics for exactly the reason recorded on op-jv1s.

WHAT STEP 5 NEEDS NOW THAT 1-4 ARE DONE: attach ThermalScattering::from_endf_file(tsl-crystalline-graphite.endf, 30, T, ...) to the carbon nuclide of the pebble/matrix material via Nuclide::with_thermal_scattering, at the material temperature; confirm the delta-tracking majorant still bounds Sigma_t once the bound channel raises it below 4 eV (sigma_total per carbon goes 4.73-5.04 b across the thermal range vs the free-gas WMP 4.74-8.99 b, so the majorant needs checking, not assuming); then a thermal-spectrum V&V case. COST WARNING from op-jv1s still applies: thermal neutrons in graphite scatter hundreds of times per history.

Also relevant: op-cjw.22 (inelastic temperature interpolation) is ADDRESSED and committed, so the re-prioritisation note at the bottom of this description is now stale - 393 K and 523 K interpolate rather than snapping, verified through the transport surface at 4.3849 and 4.1672 b (sigma_coh_el) / 0.6779 and 0.9445 b (sigma_inel).

notes.content: Coordinator note, 2026-08-11: step 4 (op-nhoa, the graphite thermal-elastic channel into transport) is COMMITTED and PUSHED as 67ebcd6c on develop, independently verified (outram-mc 254/0, njoy 455/0, Android --all-targets clean). Step 5 remains OPEN and untouched: pebble_beds/ still has zero references to thermal scattering, so htr10_fuel_zone_kinf and everything on run_keff_delta are still free-gas and still disqualified as physics. Carry forward two warnings into step 5 — (1) the delta-tracking majorant must be RE-CHECKED rather than assumed now that the bound channel raises Sigma_t below 4 eV, because a wrong Woodcock majorant is a silent bias and not a crash; (2) no k_eff has yet been computed with the elastic channel in place, so there is no end-to-end number for this epic yet.

title: HTR-10 neutronics: graphite S(alpha,beta) end-to-end — no thermal scattering law reaches the pebble-bed transport path at all

description:
FILED 2026-08-11. Two agents landed overlapping mathematics in this crate on the same day; they must be reconciled rather than left as duplicates.

WORK A (op-fm5, landed, uncommitted in tree): every transfer-function block in BOTH tiers now advances by the exact zero-order-hold / step-invariant discrete equivalent, hand-derived per block. Lives in:
  src/lib/alpha_nightly/stable_transfer_functions/{first_order_transfer_fn,first_order_transfer_fn_with_zeroes,second_order_transfer_fn,decaying_sinusoid,decaying_exponentials}.rs
  src/lib/beta_testing/stable_transfer_functions/{same, minus decaying_exponentials}.rs
  verification + O(1) regression tests: */stable_transfer_functions/recurrence_tests.rs
Each carries a module doc deriving Phi = exp(A T), Gamma = integral_0^T exp(A s) ds * B and citing Astrom & Wittenmark, Seborg et al., Franklin/Powell/Workman, Ogata, Hochbruck & Ostermann, Oppenheim & Schafer, and Smith (open access). No editions/years/pages -- none verified against a physical copy, and that constraint should be kept.

WORK B (concurrent, same day): a z_domain module ported from the GNU Octave control package (GPLv3-or-later), including c2d. That is the SAME transformation, generically implemented.

THE QUESTION TO SETTLE: should the hand-derived per-block recurrences call into z_domain::c2d, or stay as they are?
Arguments for keeping them as-is: they are exact closed forms specialised per block (2-3 scalars, no matrix algebra, no allocation), they are what makes the 0.17 us/step figure possible, and they are already verified against the analytic superposition to ~1e-15. Routing them through a general c2d would likely cost performance and would put an Octave-derived GPL port on the hot path of every controller step.
Arguments for reconciling: one source of truth for the discretisation, and z_domain::c2d could be VERIFIED AGAINST the per-block closed forms -- which is probably the real win here, and is cheap: the recurrence_tests.rs analytic-superposition harness can be pointed at c2d output directly.

RECOMMENDED: keep the specialised recurrences on the hot path; add a cross-check test that z_domain::c2d reproduces them for a first-order lag and for all three second-order damping regimes. That gives the shared-truth benefit with no performance cost.

ALSO CHECK: LICENCE PROVENANCE. The crate was relicensed Apache-2.0 -> GPL-3.0-only on 2026-08-11. The op-fm5 recurrences are original work (derived from textbook-standard mathematics, nothing copied) and carry no upstream provenance. The z_domain code IS an Octave port and needs its NOTICE/attribution-header treatment kept intact per the workspace rule. Do not let a later refactor blur which files are which.
title: chem-eng: reconcile the new z_domain c2d port with the ZOH recurrences already in stable_transfer_functions
